newsitem.title: UK: B&N to spin off Swedish Orient Lines.
newsitem.headline: B&N to spin off Swedish Orient Lines.

text.p: Bylock & Nordsjofrakt, the Swedish shipping group, said on Friday it would spin off its subsidiary Swedish Orient Lines AB through a flotation on the Stockholm stock market.
Some 75 percent of shares in the firm will be sold to investors, with priority being given to current Bylock & Nordsjofrakt shareholders, the company said.
The remaining 25 percent will be retained by the parent company.
It will be the second Bylock & Nordsjofrakt subsidiary spun-off this year as part of group strategy to release shareholder value.
Gorthon Lines, a specialist forest products shipping company, debuted on Stockholm's OTC section on June 6.
"The board has taken a decision today to proceed with the demerger of Swedish Orient Line," Bylock & Nordsjofrakt finance director Hans Carlweitz told Reuters.
Swedish Orient Lines has total assets of around 1.2 billion Swedish crowns, he said, with one billion crowns of the total accounted for by its fleet of ten vessels.
The firm operates six refrigerated ships and four roll on-roll off freight ferries.
A prospectus for the issue will be sent to shareholders at the end of September.
